title: Ramsey properties for tilings in random graphs
summary: Let $mH$ be the graph formed by $m$ vertex-disjoint copies of a graph $H$. Let $G \to (H)_r$ denote that, in any $r$-colouring of the edges of $G$, there exists a monochromatic copy of $H$. In 1975, Burr, Erdős, and Spencer showed that if $H$ is a graph on $k$ vertices whose independence number is $α$, then $K_n \to (mH)_2$, where $m\sim n/(2k-α)$, and that the $1/(2k-α)$ factor is best possible. In the 1990s, Rödl and Ruciński proved that, for all but a few graphs~$H$, the threshold for the property $\mathbb{G}(n,p) \to (H)_r$ is $n^{-1/m_2(H)}$. In this paper, generalizing the result of…
